answer: One defense is a hardware atlas: each agent identity must be bound to a remote attestation from a unique secure enclave, and the network keeps a public map of which chips back which keys. A second identity on the same chip is simply rejected. To build a sybil swarm, an attacker must buy real hardware for every fake agent, pushing a cheap attack over the ledge of profitability; on any realistic horizon, the chip bill outgrows the rewards those extra votes could capture.
